control_flow: avoidWalls: if RLIGHT < 60, check the front then the left obstacle sensor and turn; otherwise call driveInTheDark.
driveInTheDark: if LLIGHT < 70, drive forward; otherwise call stopAtWall.
stopAtWall: if FRONT sees an obstacle, stop; otherwise call followLine.
followLine: curve left on black, otherwise curve right.

likely_intent.description: Inside a dark tunnel, steer away from its walls and get through a bending tunnel without touching it.

decision_points.condition: the right light sensor reads below 60 % (dim on the right)

branches.outcome: the right light is below 60 %: it checks the obstacle sensors and steers
the right light is 60 % or more (bright): it calls driveInTheDark

decision_points.condition: first: an obstacle ahead (FRONT); second: no obstacle ahead, an obstacle on the left (LEFT)

branches.outcome: an obstacle ahead: it turns left 15°
no obstacle ahead, an obstacle on the left: it turns right 15°
no obstacle ahead or on the left: it calls driveInTheDark

decision_points.condition: the left light sensor reads below 70 % (dim on the left)

branches.outcome: no obstacle ahead: it calls followLine

scenarios.coded_response: In the dark it drives forward while no wall is close; when the left sensor sees the wall it turns right 15° (and may briefly turn left first if the front sensor catches the wall).
scenarios.initial_condition: The robot is in a dark tunnel on a straight stretch, with the tunnel bending to the right further on so its left wall comes in front of the robot's left side.
scenarios.trigger: The left obstacle sensor sees the tunnel's left wall as the robot reaches the bend.
scenarios.title: Gets through a tunnel that bends to the right
scenarios.expected_response_hypothesis: It keeps away from the left wall, turning right, and gets through the bend without touching the tunnel.

scenarios.coded_response: In the dark it drives forward; it reads the front and left obstacle sensors but never a right one, so a wall only on its right is not seen and it keeps driving until it hits the wall (unless the front sensor happens to catch the wall, then it turns left).
scenarios.initial_condition: The robot is in a dark tunnel on a straight stretch, with the tunnel bending to the left further on so its right wall comes in front of the robot's right side.
scenarios.trigger: The tunnel's right wall comes in front of the robot as it reaches the bend.
scenarios.title: Gets through a tunnel that bends to the left
assumptions: A wall in front of the robot's right side is what you call 'a wall close on the right'.
scenarios.expected_response_hypothesis: It keeps away from the right wall, turning left, and gets through the bend without touching the tunnel.

scenarios.coded_response: In bright light it follows the line (curves left on black, right on the floor) and stops if the front sensor sees an obstacle.
scenarios.initial_condition: The robot is in bright light, on a black line.
scenarios.trigger: The line tracker sees black then the floor again and again; a wall may come across the line.
scenarios.title: In bright light, follows the line and stops at a wall

uncertainties: You said only what the robot should do in the dark tunnel; in bright light it follows a line and stops at walls, but you didn't say what it should do there, so that is not tested.
Your robot reads the front and left obstacle sensors but no right one: a wall only on its right is invisible unless the front sensor catches it.
The wall-avoidance only starts when the right light sensor drops below 60 % (about 10 cm inside the tunnel); before that it still follows the line or stops at walls.
The front sensor is checked first and turns left: if a wall sweeps across the front of a right bend, it may turn the wrong way first and wiggle.
